newsitem.title: USA: GM to consolidate metal fabricating in Flint.
newsitem.headline: GM to consolidate metal fabricating in Flint.

text.p: General Motors Corp said its Metal Fabricating Division will consolidate its headquarters from two Troy, Mich. locations to the Great Lakes Technology Centre in Flint, Mich.
The move will occur in late 1999 or early 2000, GM said.
"The consolidation brings about 1,000 jobs to Flint and strengthens the division's ability to be more competitive," said the world's largest automaker.
The Metal Fabricating Division employs 1,003 people at two buildings in Troy.

The Metal Fabricating Division consists of 14 metal fabricating facilities -- six which include die operations -- with additional responsibility for four contiguous stamping operations in Doraville, Ga., Fairfax, Kans., Oshawa. Ont., and Wentzville, Mo., and the Flint Tool and Die Shop.
Nationally, the division's 34,000 employees process an average of 1.7 million tons of steel for GM cars and trucks each year, the company said.
